tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: I wonder where he is.
I wonder where is he.
Could you tell me what time the meeting starts?
Could you tell me what time does the meeting start?
She asked whether the figures were final.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — After wonder, the clause keeps statement order: where + subject + verb (where he is), not question inversion.

Tip: Embedded wh-clauses look like statements, not questions.

FALSE — where is he inverts auxiliary and subject, which belongs in a direct question, not after I wonder.

Tip: Drop the inversion: where he is.

TRUE — Polite frame Could you tell me… embeds what time the meeting starts with subject before the verb.

Tip: No does inside the embedded clause.

FALSE — does the meeting start is direct-question word order jammed into an indirect question.

Tip: Use what time the meeting starts.

TRUE — whether correctly introduces a yes/no embedded clause with statement order (the figures were).

Tip: whether/if + subject + verb — never invert.
tasks.solution_overview: Indirect questions keep statement word order after the question word or whether/if. Scan for stray do/does/did or swapped auxiliary–subject pairs — those belong only in direct questions.

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Do you know if the report has been filed?
Do you know if has the report been filed?
Please explain why costs rose.
Please explain why did costs rise.
They could not decide which option was safer.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — if embeds a yes/no clause with normal order: the report has been filed.

Tip: After if/whether, never move has/is/will before the subject.

FALSE — if has the report… wrongly inverts the auxiliary into the embedded clause.

Tip: Keep if the report has…

TRUE — why costs rose is statement order after explain; no auxiliary is needed.

Tip: Embedded why-clauses do not take did unless the original had do-support for another reason.

FALSE — why did costs rise mirrors a direct question; the embedding verb already carries the interrogative force.

Tip: why + subject + past: why costs rose.

TRUE — which option was safer keeps subject–verb order inside the embedded choice question.

Tip: which + noun + verb — no extra it.
tasks.solution_overview: Focus on if/whether and wh-clauses after know, explain, and decide. Correct items keep subject before the finite verb; wrong ones smuggle direct-question inversion (has…?, did…?) into the subordinate clause.

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The question is how the firm will respond.
The question is how will the firm respond?
I am not sure what caused the outage.
I am not sure what did cause the outage.
She asked whether were the figures final.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — After The question is, how the firm will respond uses statement order (subject firm before will).

Tip: Noun-phrase frames still take embedded statement order.

FALSE — how will the firm respond? is a direct question glued onto The question is.

Tip: how + subject + modal: how the firm will respond.

TRUE — what is the subject of caused, so no do-support is required or allowed.

Tip: Subject wh-clauses never need did.

FALSE — what did cause forces unnecessary do-support into an embedded subject question.

Tip: what caused, not what did cause.

FALSE — whether were the figures… inverts were and the subject after whether.

Tip: whether the figures were…
tasks.solution_overview: Watch two classic traps: modal inversion after how (will the firm…) and fake did in subject questions (what did cause…). Correct embedded clauses read like calm statements inside a larger sentence.

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: They could not decide which option was it safer.
I'd like to know when the auditors arrive.
I'd like to know when do the auditors arrive.
Can you remind me where the spare keys are kept?
Can you remind me where are the spare keys kept?
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Extra pronoun it after was breaks the clause; which option was safer is already complete.

Tip: Never add a dummy it after the verb in an embedded which-clause.

TRUE — when the auditors arrive keeps subject–verb order after I'd like to know.

Tip: Softeners like I'd like to know still take statement order.

FALSE — when do the auditors arrive inserts do-support as if the clause were a direct question.

Tip: Delete do: when the auditors arrive.

TRUE — where the spare keys are kept is passive statement order inside a polite question.

Tip: are stays after the subject keys.

FALSE — where are the spare keys… flips are before the subject inside the embedded clause.

Tip: where + subject + are/is…
highlights: where the spare keys are kept
tasks.solution_overview: Polite frames (I'd like to know, Can you remind me) do not license inversion inside the embedded clause. Also reject dummy it after which… was — the option is already the subject.

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Nobody could say who had authorised the transfer.
Nobody could say who had the transfer been authorised by.
We need to establish whether the supplier can meet the deadline.
We need to establish whether can the supplier meet the deadline.
Tell me how much the upgrade will cost.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — who is subject of had authorised; statement order is natural and correct.

Tip: Subject who/what never invert with the verb.

FALSE — who had the transfer been… forces awkward inversion and a stranded by that belongs in a rewritten object question.

Tip: Prefer who had authorised… or by whom the transfer had been authorised.

TRUE — whether the supplier can meet… keeps modal can after the subject.

Tip: whether + subject + modal + verb.

FALSE — whether can the supplier… is direct yes/no inversion after whether.

Tip: Never put the modal before the subject in an embedded clause.

TRUE — how much the upgrade will cost is statement order after Tell me.

Tip: how much/how many + noun phrase + verb — no will-fronting.
highlights: how much the upgrade will cost
tasks.solution_overview: Subject wh-words (who authorised…) stay simple; modal yes/no embeds keep can/will after the subject. Reject any whether can… or how much will… fronting inside the subordinate clause.

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Tell me how much will the upgrade cost.
The memo does not say how long the outage lasted.
The memo does not say how long did the outage last.
Investors asked what the board intended to do next.
Investors asked what did the board intend to do next.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — how much will the upgrade cost inverts will and the subject after Tell me.

Tip: how much the upgrade will cost.

TRUE — how long the outage lasted is a clean embedded duration clause.

Tip: how long + subject + past verb.

FALSE — how long did the outage last imports direct-question did.

Tip: Drop did and keep past simple: lasted.

TRUE — what the board intended… places the subject board before the verb.

Tip: Object what still uses statement order: what + subject + verb.

FALSE — what did the board intend… is a direct object question pattern inside reported asking.

Tip: what the board intended / what the board intends.
tasks.solution_overview: how much, how long, and object what all take statement order once embedded. Any will/did sitting before the subject is a leftover from a direct question — delete the fronted auxiliary.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Have you checked whether the invoices match the purchase orders?
Have you checked whether do the invoices match the purchase orders?
I'm curious who she nominated for the panel.
I'm curious who did she nominate for the panel.
The brief should clarify which metrics matter most.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — whether the invoices match… is statement order under a yes/no main question.

Tip: The outer Have you…? does not license inversion inside whether…

FALSE — whether do the invoices… adds illegal do-support after whether.

Tip: whether + subject + verb.

TRUE — who is the object of nominated; she stays before the verb in embedded order.

Tip: Object who: who + subject + verb.

FALSE — who did she nominate is direct-question order after I'm curious.

Tip: who she nominated.

TRUE — which metrics matter most needs no auxiliary; metrics is the subject.

Tip: Subject which-phrases never take do.
tasks.solution_overview: Separate subject who/which (no do) from object who (who + subject + verb). Outer question marks on Have you…? never justify do or inversion after whether or who inside the embed.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The brief should clarify which metrics do matter most.
Staff were unsure where to send the revised draft.
Staff were unsure where should they send the revised draft.
Could you confirm if payroll has processed the bonus?
Could you confirm if has payroll processed the bonus?
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — which metrics do matter adds emphatic do that is unnecessary and exam-wrong in a neutral embed.

Tip: which metrics matter — no do.

TRUE — where to send… is a correct infinitive indirect question (no subject inversion possible).

Tip: wh- + to-infinitive is a standard compact embed.

FALSE — where should they send… inverts modal and subject as in a direct question.

Tip: where they should send… or where to send…

TRUE — if payroll has processed… keeps perfect have after the subject.

Tip: if/whether + subject + has/have…

FALSE — if has payroll… front-loads has before the subject.

Tip: Move has after payroll.
tasks.solution_overview: Infinitive embeds (where to send) are a safe alternative to full clauses. When you use a full clause, keep modals and have/has after the subject — never before.

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: We still do not know whose proposal the committee selected.
We still do not know whose proposal did the committee select.
It remains unclear how the breach was discovered.
It remains unclear how was the breach discovered.
Ask her whether she can join the noon call.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — whose proposal the committee selected keeps the subject committee before selected.

Tip: whose + noun + subject + verb.

FALSE — whose proposal did the committee select is direct-question do-support.

Tip: Drop did: whose proposal the committee selected.

TRUE — how the breach was discovered is passive statement order under It remains unclear.

Tip: Passive embeds still put was after the subject.

FALSE — how was the breach discovered inverts was into question position.

Tip: how the breach was discovered.

TRUE — whether she can join… is a clean yes/no embed after Ask.

Tip: Ask + whether/if + statement order.
tasks.solution_overview: whose and passive how-clauses follow the same rule as simpler embeds: subject before the finite verb. Frames like It remains unclear or Ask her do not change that order.

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Ask her whether can she join the noon call.
The clients want to know what we are offering this quarter.
The clients want to know what are we offering this quarter.
No one has confirmed who will chair the session.
No one has confirmed who will the session be chaired by.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — whether can she… inverts can and she after whether.

Tip: whether she can…

TRUE — what we are offering keeps progressive are after the subject we.

Tip: Continuous embeds: what + subject + are/is + -ing.

FALSE — what are we offering is direct continuous-question order.

Tip: what we are offering.

TRUE — who will chair… treats who as subject; will stays after who.

Tip: Subject who + modal + verb is already statement-shaped.

FALSE — who will the session be chaired by awkwardly inverts and strands by; prefer who will chair… or by whom the session will be chaired.

Tip: Avoid forcing object-passive word order when a subject who is available.
tasks.solution_overview: Progressive and modal embeds fail the same way: are/will jumps before the subject. Prefer a subject who-clause (who will chair…) over a clunky inverted passive with stranded by.

tasks.title: Task 11
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Please let us know if you require further documentation.
Please let us know if do you require further documentation.
I cannot recall why the previous vendor was dropped.
I cannot recall why was the previous vendor dropped.
They debated whether to accept the counter-offer.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — if you require… is standard polite statement order after let us know.

Tip: Business closers still embed, not invert.

FALSE — if do you require… mixes a direct question into the embed.

Tip: Delete do you → if you require.

TRUE — why the previous vendor was dropped keeps passive was after the subject.

Tip: why + subject + was/were + PP.

FALSE — why was the previous vendor dropped is direct-question inversion.

Tip: why the previous vendor was dropped.

TRUE — whether to accept… is a correct infinitive yes/no embed (no subject to invert).

Tip: whether to + verb is standard for undecided choices.
highlights: why the previous vendor was dropped
tasks.solution_overview: Email-style if-clauses and why-passives must stay uninverted. whether to + infinitive is a third lawful shape — compact and free of subject–auxiliary swapping.

tasks.title: Task 12
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: They debated whether should they accept the counter-offer.
She wondered how many seats were still available.
She wondered how many seats were there still available.
Do you remember what the password hint was?
Do you remember what was the password hint?
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — whether should they… inverts the modal; use whether they should… or whether to accept…

Tip: Full clause: whether + subject + modal.

TRUE — how many seats were still available places were after seats.

Tip: how many + noun + verb.

FALSE — were there is an existential inversion pattern that does not belong after wondered how many seats…

Tip: Avoid there-inversion inside how many embeds.

TRUE — what the password hint was puts was at the end in statement order (subject hint before was).

Tip: Embedded what… was keeps be last.

FALSE — what was the password hint? is direct-question be-fronting after remember.

Tip: what the password hint was.
tasks.solution_overview: Be-fronting (what was…?) and there-inversion (were there…?) are direct-question habits. Inside embeds, leave was/were after the real subject, and keep whether + subject + modal.

tasks.title: Task 13
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The analyst could not determine from which sources the rumour originated.
The analyst could not determine from which sources did the rumour originate.
We are assessing what impact the delay may have on delivery.
We are assessing what impact may the delay have on delivery.
Kindly advise when the signed copies will be returned.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Formal pied-piping from which sources the rumour originated keeps statement order after the prepositional wh-phrase.

Tip: Preposition + which + subject + verb is fine in formal embeds.

FALSE — …sources did the rumour originate adds do-support as in a direct question.

Tip: originated without did.

TRUE — what impact the delay may have keeps may after the subject delay.

Tip: what + noun + subject + modal + verb.

FALSE — what impact may the delay have front-loads may before the subject.

Tip: the delay may have, not may the delay have.

TRUE — when the signed copies will be returned is passive statement order after Kindly advise.

Tip: will stays after the subject copies.
highlights: from which sources the rumour originated
what impact the delay may have
when the signed copies will be returned
tasks.solution_overview: Formal prepositional wh-phrases and what + noun objects still forbid do-support and modal fronting. Read the embedded string aloud: if it sounds like a stand-alone question, the word order is probably wrong.

tasks.title: Task 14
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Kindly advise when will the signed copies be returned.
It is unclear to whom the confidential annex was circulated.
It is unclear to whom was the confidential annex circulated.
Management queried how often the backups are tested.
Management queried how often are the backups tested.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — when will the signed copies… inverts will after Kindly advise.

Tip: when the signed copies will…

TRUE — Formal to whom the confidential annex was circulated keeps was after the subject.

Tip: to whom + subject + verb (formal object question).

FALSE — to whom was the confidential annex… inverts was into question position.

Tip: Keep was after annex.

TRUE — how often the backups are tested is statement order for frequency embeds.

Tip: how often + subject + verb.

FALSE — how often are the backups tested is direct-question inversion.

Tip: how often the backups are tested.
highlights: to whom the confidential annex was
how often the backups are tested
tasks.solution_overview: Formal whom-phrases and how often-clauses still use statement order. Inversion after to whom or how often is a direct-question reflex — wrong once the clause is embedded.

tasks.title: Task 15
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The auditor asked under what conditions the discount would apply.
The auditor asked under what conditions would the discount apply.
Nobody knows which of the two bids the panel prefers.
Nobody knows which of the two bids does the panel prefer.
Please specify where the temporary files should be stored.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — under what conditions the discount would apply keeps would after the subject.

Tip: Long wh-phrases still take subject + modal order.

FALSE — under what conditions would the discount apply is direct modal inversion.

Tip: …conditions the discount would apply.

TRUE — which of the two bids the panel prefers places prefers after panel.

Tip: which of… + subject + verb.

FALSE — which… does the panel prefer inserts do-support.

Tip: Drop does: the panel prefers.

TRUE — where the temporary files should be stored keeps should after the subject.

Tip: where + subject + modal + be + PP.
highlights: under what conditions the discount would
which of the two bids the panel prefers
where the temporary files should be stored
tasks.solution_overview: Longer wh-openers (under what conditions, which of the two bids) tempt writers to invert as if starting a new question mid-sentence. Resist: finish with subject + verb, not would/does + subject.

tasks.title: Task 16
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Please specify where should the temporary files be stored.
Researchers examined whether or not the sample was representative.
Researchers examined whether or not was the sample representative.
I need to find out who the message was intended for.
I need to find out who was the message intended for.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — where should the temporary files… inverts should after specify.

Tip: where the temporary files should…

TRUE — whether or not the sample was representative is a standard yes/no embed with or not.

Tip: whether or not + subject + verb.

FALSE — whether or not was the sample… wrongly inverts was.

Tip: Keep was after sample.

TRUE — Informal stranded for is acceptable: who the message was intended for with statement order.

Tip: who + subject + was + PP + preposition.

FALSE — who was the message intended for? is direct-question be-fronting.

Tip: who the message was intended for.
highlights: whether or not the sample was
whether or not was the sample
who the message was intended for
who was the message intended for
tasks.solution_overview: whether or not does not unlock inversion. Stranded-preposition object questions (who… for) still keep was after the subject — only the outer sentence may look interrogative.

tasks.title: Task 17
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The board inquired how soon a revised forecast could be produced.
The board inquired how soon could a revised forecast be produced.
It is debatable whether such a clause should even be included.
It is debatable whether should such a clause even be included.
Few partners recalled what assumptions underpinned the valuation model.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — how soon a revised forecast could be produced keeps could after the subject.

Tip: how soon/how quickly + subject + modal…

FALSE — how soon could a revised forecast… is direct modal inversion.

Tip: …forecast could be produced.

TRUE — whether such a clause should even be included is statement order with focusing even.

Tip: Adverbs like even stay inside; they do not trigger inversion.

FALSE — whether should such a clause… front-loads should before the subject.

Tip: whether such a clause should…

TRUE — what assumptions underpinned… treats what assumptions as subject — no do needed.

Tip: Subject what + noun takes the verb directly.
highlights: how soon a revised forecast could
tasks.solution_overview: Advanced how soon and whether… should embeds fail only when the modal jumps left of the subject. Subject what-noun phrases (what assumptions underpinned…) remain do-free.

tasks.title: Task 18
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Few partners recalled what assumptions did underpin the valuation model.
Counsel sought clarification as to why the indemnity had been narrowed.
Counsel sought clarification as to why had the indemnity been narrowed.
The survey asked respondents how satisfied they were with remote support.
The survey asked respondents how satisfied were they with remote support.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — what assumptions did underpin… inserts unnecessary did into a subject clause.

Tip: what assumptions underpinned…

TRUE — as to why the indemnity had been narrowed is a formal embed with past perfect passive statement order.

Tip: as to why + subject + had been + PP.

FALSE — as to why had the indemnity… inverts had before the subject.

Tip: why the indemnity had been…

TRUE — how satisfied they were… is the standard adjectival how-clause order.

Tip: how + adjective + subject + be.

FALSE — how satisfied were they… is direct-question be-inversion.

Tip: how satisfied they were…
highlights: why the indemnity had been narrowed
tasks.solution_overview: Formal as to why and survey how + adjective patterns still ban auxiliary fronting. Fake did in subject what-clauses is another advanced trap — delete it.

tasks.title: Task 19
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Regulators questioned on what basis the exemption had been granted.
Regulators questioned on what basis had the exemption been granted.
We must decide which vendor we should engage first.
We must decide which vendor should we engage first.
The minutes do not record who seconded the motion.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — on what basis the exemption had been granted keeps had after the subject.

Tip: on what basis/grounds + subject + verb.

FALSE — on what basis had the exemption… is direct perfect inversion.

Tip: …basis the exemption had been granted.

TRUE — which vendor we should engage first keeps should after we.

Tip: which + noun + subject + modal + verb.

FALSE — which vendor should we engage is direct-question order after decide.

Tip: which vendor we should engage.

TRUE — who seconded the motion is a subject clause with no inversion and no do.

Tip: Subject who + past verb.
highlights: on what basis the exemption had
on what basis had the exemption
tasks.solution_overview: Prepositional wh-openers (on what basis) and object which-clauses (which vendor we should…) both fail when the auxiliary precedes the subject. Subject who remains the simplest correct pattern.

tasks.title: Task 20
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The minutes do not record who did second the motion.
Partners remain divided over whether the spin-off itself makes strategic sense.
Partners remain divided over whether does the spin-off itself make strategic sense.
I wonder where the CFO is during the blackout window.
I wonder where is the CFO during the blackout window.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — who did second… adds emphatic/wrong do to a subject question.

Tip: who seconded — never who did second in this embed.

TRUE — whether the spin-off itself makes… keeps makes after the subject; itself is just a focusing pronoun.

Tip: Extra focus words do not change embedded order.

FALSE — whether does the spin-off… invents do-support after whether.

Tip: whether the spin-off makes…

TRUE — where the CFO is… is the classic wonder pattern with statement order.

Tip: I wonder where + subject + is.

FALSE — where is the CFO… reverts to direct-question inversion after wonder.

Tip: where the CFO is — the core contrast of this topic.
tasks.solution_overview: Close on the signature contrast: wonder where the CFO is (statement order) versus where is the CFO (direct inversion). Along the way, reject fake do after who or whether — embeds do not need it.
